english.title: Aggravated vehicle taking - ( being carried on ) and injury caused by an accident
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), knowing that a mechanically propelled vehicle, namely **(..SPECIFY VEHICLE MAKE AND INDEX NUMBER..), had been taken without the consent of the owner or other lawful authority, allowed yourself to be carried in or on the said vehicle, and after the vehicle was unlawfully taken and before it was recovered, owing to the driving of the vehicle, an accident occurred by which injury was caused to **(..SPECIFY THE PERSON OR PERSONS..).

(A)_[There were no other additional aggravating factors]_
(B)_[Additional aggravating factors were **(..SPECIFY THE FACTORS..)]_
english.legislation: Contrary to section 12A of the Theft Act 1968.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
knowing a mechanically propelled vehicle
had been taken without owner's consent/other lawful authority
allowed yourself to be carried (NOT being the initial taker OR a subsequent driver)
in/on the vehicle and after the vehicle had been taken and before it was recovered
owing to the driving of the vehicle an accident occurred by which injury was caused

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Mandatory drug test required if 18 or over
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) This wording is for use ONLY were the defendant was a 'PERSON BEING CARRIED ON' - for the 'initial taker' see H4383 and 'subsequent driver' see H4386.
(ii) More than one person may be named.
(iii) See also H4393, H4388, H4390, H4486, H4487 and H4488 for other aggravated vehicle taking wordings relating to a 'person being carried on'.

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
INDICTMENT: Two years imprisonment and / or unlimited fine.

Obligatory disqualification and endorsement.

Obligatory endorsement - licence endorsed three to eleven penalty points - only if special reasons apply.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
